solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

blocks.note: ex = former, old
an acting head is a deputy standing in

annotation.surface: A description of a hardened former second-in-command.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tough old' reads as one phrase about a person; it splits after 'Tough', and 'deputy' works as an adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an exacting task or boss is tough, demanding a great deal.

entries.clue: Type of car in Orient Express? (6)

blocks.note: the Orient is the East, E
to state = to express

annotation.surface: Asks what sort of carriage runs on the famous Orient Express train.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital letters make 'Orient Express' look like the train; split, it is East plus a verb. An estate car is the British name for a station wagon.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: in Britain an estate is a car with a long body and rear door, what Americans call a station wagon.

blocks.note: the boy wizard's family car, which flies in the second book
the Latin name for the land of the Angles, still in a region of eastern England

annotation.surface: Suggests a pottery wheel from some medieval land.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Potter's wheels' pulls toward the ceramics tool; it means Harry Potter's car, the flying Ford Anglia in Chamber of Secrets. East Anglia was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom in eastern England.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: the Weasleys' flying car is a Ford Anglia, and Anglia is the Latin name for the land of the Angles.

indicatorNotes.Avoiding: the word steers clear of the S, so it is left out

blocks.note: a stiff penalty is a harsh one
S = small, as on clothing labels; removed

annotation.surface: Advice to steer clear of short, cruel remarks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Words' in the plural is the definition: to have words with someone is to quarrel.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to have words is to argue, and a tiff is a minor quarrel.

indicatorNotes.letters: only the letters of 15 are used, so they may be put in any order

blocks.note: the answer to 15 across

annotation.surface: Describes a notice, perhaps on a private club door, as built from the letters of another answer.
annotation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is to 15 across; its twelve letters rearrange into the notice.
annotation.definitionFit: A notice that keeps people out is what makes a place exclusive.

blocks.note: as it stands
twill is a fabric woven with diagonal ribs

annotation.surface: The moment of picking fabric in a shop.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a question about choosing cloth; split after 'chooses', it is A plus a fabric.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: doing something at will means doing it whenever one pleases.

entries.clue: Barking pet is only a dog (3,7)

indicatorNotes.Barking: barking = mad, so the letters go crazy

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

annotation.surface: A grudging remark that the noisy pet is just a dog after all.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Barking' looks like the dog making noise; it is the British slang for mad, as in 'barking mad'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by genus: a toy spaniel is a small breed of spaniel kept as a lapdog.

blocks.note: someone just admitted to a society after its rites
a verb here: to start something off

annotation.surface: Two ways of describing a newcomer to a society.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pioneer' reads as a noun alongside 'New member'; it is a verb, and the answer changes stress to match.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: the noun for a newly admitted member, and the verb for beginning something new.

indicatorNotes.not opening: the word is used without its opening letter

blocks.note: a platitude is a trite, corny remark
P removed from the front

annotation.surface: A cheesy line that doesn't feature at the start of a drama.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a stage show; it means room to move, as in play in a rope.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean freedom of action or scope allowed.

entries.clue: Backing more wins in this game (3,2,3)

annotation.definition: Backing more wins in this game

blocks.note: surface reading: putting more money on a bet; setter's reading: going backwards further
in a rope-pulling contest, the team that retreats drags the other over the line

annotation.surface: Sounds like a betting tip: put more money on and you win.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backing' suggests gambling support; in a tug of war the team that moves backwards furthest wins.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes the contest: two teams pull a rope, and the side that retreats takes the prize.

entries.clue: Year in schedule for Apollo, say (6)

indicatorNotes.in: the year goes in the schedule

blocks.note: a schedule is a list; it goes round
yr = year

annotation.surface: A timetable slot booked for a NASA mission.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Apollo' pulls toward the space programme; it is the Greek god of music, who played the lyre.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Apollo, god of music, played the lyre, so he is one instance of a lyre player.

blocks.note: surface reading: journeying with little luggage; setter's reading: a flame that travels
it is carried in relay until it arrives at the Games' opening ceremony

annotation.surface: Sounds like packing little luggage for a sporting trip.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Travelling light' is the idiom for carrying little baggage; here it is a literal light that travels, carried in relay to the host city of the Games.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads literally: a flame carried across countries to arrive at the opening of the Games.

indicatorNotes.Somewhat: only some of the words are used

blocks.note: lefT-WINg

annotation.surface: Calls the satirical puppet show Spitting Image a bit leftish.
annotation.walkthrough: Spitting Image was a British TV satire using latex puppets of politicians; here the phrase just means an exact likeness.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'the spitting image' of someone is their exact double, which an identical twin is.

entries.clue: Diminutive type taking run around arcade (5,5)

indicatorNotes.around: the run goes around the arcade

blocks.note: to sprint is to run; it goes round
a shopping arcade is a mall

annotation.surface: A small person jogging around a shopping centre.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Diminutive type' looks like a short person; it means lettering in a tiny font.
annotation.definitionFit: A literal reading: text set in tiny type, often hiding the conditions of a contract.

blocks.note: a jolly is a party or outing
radio-speak for 'message understood'

annotation.surface: Someone agreeing that it's just an ordinary party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Standard' reads as 'ordinary'; it is a flag. A jolly is British slang for a fun outing.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a standard is a flag, and the pirates' skull and crossbones is one.

indicatorNotes.Tainted: tainted = corrupted, so the letters are spoiled out of order

blocks.note: the answer to 19 down
as printed

annotation.surface: Something spoiled made a thing unclean.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tainted' looks like the definition, sitting first; it is the anagram signal, and the definition is 'impure' at the end.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something impure has been spoiled by foreign matter.

indicatorNotes.announced: an announcement is spoken, so we go by sound

blocks.note: a rein is a check or arrest, so 'an arrest's' = 'a rein's'

annotation.surface: Formal charges being read out at the moment of arrest.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is courtroom procedure, and so is the answer; the trick is reading 'an arrest' as 'a rein', a restraint.
annotation.definitionFit: A legal sense: to call someone before a court to answer formal charges.

indicatorNotes.Radical: radical = drastic change, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.ignores: the letters of MP'S are left out

blocks.note: the word as printed
M, P and S removed, leaving YATHISER

annotation.surface: A left-wing supporter shrugging off a politician's fuss.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Radical sympathiser' reads as a political supporter; 'Radical' is the anagram signal, working on what is left once M, P and an S go.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: extreme, uncontrolled emotional excitement.

indicatorNotes.manoeuvres: the letters are moved about like troops

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

annotation.surface: A news line about troops exercising in Israel.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the Royal Marines are a fighting force who could be on manoeuvres; the question mark admits they are not strictly an army.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue describes Britain's amphibious infantry out on exercise, a force that goes on military manoeuvres.

entries.clue: Is unable to find “forget it” in slang (6)

indicatorNotes.in: the refusal goes inside the slang

blocks.note: cant is jargon or slang; it goes round
'no' as a flat refusal

annotation.surface: Someone failing to locate a slang expression for 'forget it'.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition runs past the natural break: 'Is unable to' is the answer, and 'find' only joins.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the negative of 'can', which means 'is able to'.

indicatorNotes.called: called = said out loud, so the words are heard

blocks.note: too = also; the can is slang for prison

annotation.surface: A bird that also goes by the name of a jail.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Also called' reads as 'otherwise known as'; 'called' is actually the sound signal applied to 'also' plus 'prison'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by genus: a tropical bird with an enormous bill.

entries.clue: Fuel modern technology in an ancient country (10)

indicatorNotes.in: the technology goes in the country

blocks.note: as it stands
Thrace, an ancient land north of the Aegean; it goes round
IT = information technology

annotation.surface: Powering new tech somewhere in the classical world.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fuel' looks like a verb; it is the noun for the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by genus: a hard, clean-burning coal burnt as fuel.

blocks.note: pop = father
O = over, the cricket abbreviation

annotation.surface: Instructions to hop over a low wall.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pop over' reads as a verb phrase; 'Pop' is father and 'over' is O.
annotation.definitionFit: A literal description: the lower part of an interior wall, often panelled differently from above.

blocks.note: to get on, as in 'how did you get on?'
the food offered, as in 'simple country food'

annotation.surface: Someone urging a guest to try the food.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Go on' reads as encouragement; it means get on, as in how things go.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: the verb for getting along, and the noun for food on the table, as in 'bill of fare'.

entries.clue: Book taken from junk shop for repair (6)

indicatorNotes.taken from: the B is removed from the junk

blocks.note: garbage = junk
B = book; removed

annotation.surface: A volume picked up from a second-hand shop to be mended.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Junk shop' reads as one phrase; it splits, with 'shop for repair' the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A literal description: a workshop where cars are mended.

indicatorNotes.Silly: the letters are made foolish, jumbled

blocks.note: the word itself is the fodder
C = cold, as on taps

annotation.surface: A setter mocking their own feeble anagram before a cold drink.
annotation.walkthrough: The word 'anagram' looks like a comment on the clue; it is itself the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by genus: a brandy from Gascony in France.

indicatorNotes.finally: 'finally' means at the end, so only the end of 'Eyes' is used

blocks.note: last letter of eyeS
to tarry is to stop or linger

annotation.surface: Eyes that at last cease sparkling.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stop twinkling' reads as one instruction; the definition is 'twinkling' alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: a sky full of stars twinkles, and bright eyes are called starry.

entries.clue: Yarn cut by late morning for loom (8)

indicatorNotes.cut: the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: THREAD without its last letter
ten o'clock

annotation.surface: Thread snipped by a weaver late in the morning, for the loom.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Loom' looks like the weaving frame, fitting the yarn; it is the verb, to hang over menacingly.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: storm clouds that loom hang over ominously, as danger does.
